metadata.title: Unclaimed Estates & Abandoned Properties in Spain - tracing Heirs Worldwide
metadata.author: My Lawyer In Spain
metadata.shortDescription:
What happens to unclaimed estates and abandoned properties in Spain or abroad? In this episode, Alex Radford of My Lawyer in Spain was joined by Ryan Gregory and Sophie Smith from Finders International, the award-winning probate genealogy firm featured on BBC’s Heir Hunters.

Together they discuss how Finders International locates missing heirs, recovers unclaimed assets and brings long-forgotten properties back to life.

If you’ve ever wondered what happens when someone dies without a will, how international probate tracing works, or how to recover abandoned property in Spain, this video is a must-watch.


🔗 Useful Links:

Finders International – https://www.findersinternational.co.uk

My Lawyer in Spain – https://www.mylawyerinspain.com



#UnclaimedEstates #FindersInternational #MyLawyerInSpain #SpanishInheritance #HeirTracing #AbandonedPropertySpain #InternationalProbate #HeirHunters #EstatePlanning #SpanishLaw #InheritanceInSpain

segments.text: Hey, good afternoon everyone and welcome to another session with My Lawyer in Spain and
today I'm really delighted we've got Sophie and Ryan joining us from Finders International. How
are you both? Good, thanks Alex. Thanks for having us. Oh, thank you for coming on board. Thank you
for coming on board. So today we're basically going to be talking about unclaimed estates
and abandoned properties and how an organisation like uh Finders could help you um search for those
beneficiaries or heirs or they may even knock on your door and say you've they found some a long
distant cousin that you didn't know you had and uh they've left kind of left you some money. So
um that's basically um what we're going to be talking about today. Do you want to just give us
a brief overview of Finders and what you actually do? Yes, again, thanks for having us, Alex. Uh, my
name is Ryan Gregory, the international manager at Finders International. I'm here with Sophie Smith,
who's our key account manager, and she handles cases from Spain and across the Spanish diaspora
across the world. She's our Spanish specialist. Um, so a little bit about Finders International.
We've been around since 1997. We primarily locate beneficiaries to intestate and testate
estates also missing owners of dormant assets or unclaimed property as it's known in some
countries. Uh family tree verific verification is a big part of what we do as well as I would add
um over the years anything which may be considered positive tracing as long as there's a positive
reason usually financial for the person to be traced. We have uh a very thorough UK network
in-house genealogologists and researchers and an international network overseas that can pretty
much track anyone anywhere in the world. Wow. So, um so you guys are quite busy there. There's never
a quiet day, is there Sophie? to be fair like the case managers especially will know how busy it is
and you know with a you know tens or scores of cases at any one time and um millions of pounds
worth of assets on the books to try and find heirs too. It's um it's it's a busy it's it's
a niche industry as you probably pointed to at the beginning and a lot of people haven't heard about
what we do but it's very very busy especially at Finders at this time. Okay. Excellent. So, you
know, you know, the challenges of filing unclaimed estates and abandoned properties. Talk to us about
that. I mean, how big an issue is that? It's a growing issue. Um, in the UK, we've been on
top of the issue for quite a while. We work with local authorities. Um, they have empty property
departments, some of them empty home departments. uh that in the UK at least will be sometimes the
first port of call where it could flag to a firm such as finders where there is someone that's
passed away. There are other avenues similar in Spain, you know, there's the private client arena
where some private client solicitor may come to us and instructs us on an intestate case or someone's
drafted a will and it says to John Smith who lives down the street 20 years ago without putting a
door number, which is always a a great case to try and crack. Um so it could be testate or intestate
and we could get referrals from local authorities, nursing homes, hospitals, um private clients,
other probate research companies overseas. Um and particularly in Spain, we do have a a bulk of work
which comes from Spain and it is primarily due to these properties that have been vacant for a long
time. I mean, yes, that could be because someone came to buy a property before COVID and hasn't
gone back or they've kind of gone into a nursing home here in the UK and they haven't gone back
to Spain. But sometimes we're finding that someone has passed away in Spain within a matter of months
or years. The property hasn't been dealt with and it's just left there dormant and, you know,
attracting squatters or vermin or vandals. And um Sophie especially is on the kind of
receiving end of those type of cases. So, we kind of feel like we're doing a something good for the
community in order to get these properties back into play, back into kind of private ownership,
but also on the back end of that, we're tracing the beneficiaries who should stand to inherit from
their deceased relatives estate. Wow. And that moment when you contact, you know, a beneficiary
and tell them that they're entitled something. I mean, could just talk us through that? It can
go one of a few ways. Um, one, someone puts the phone down. That's quite common. Um, you know,
someone will think it's a fake sales call. A lot of what we do is is cold calling. Um, you know,
sometimes you can write letters and you don't know whether they arrived or you don't know if
someone's moved on. Um, so we're kind of bringing people out of the blue quite a lot. We also in the
UK and Ireland have a network of representatives, their ex police officers primarily that can go and
visit people, you know, twofold as well, to deliver sensitive news. Um obviously they're
trained in that and also you know trying to find out exactly that has someone moved recently so our
databases haven't been updated have they passed away are they in hospital are they on holiday
um those sort of things so door-to-door inquiries is very much kind of boots on the ground in the
UK but also internationally we're finding a lot of the countries we work in be it South America
Africa um boots on the ground is often the only way to really do it so we are utilising local
agents in a lot of areas around the world at any one time, knocking on doors and just doing
traditional kind of detective investigation work. Yeah. So, and and and and so what limitations
are there? I mean, how far can you go? Um what's kind of holding you back? Um well,
talking about international work, um which is obviously our bread and butter of Sophia and mine,
the limitations are quite numerous. Um often we receive a case and very much from the start we
are very limited in information that we have for some for instance often we'll just have
a name a date of birth a date of death obviously a place of death and then sometimes the date of
the place of birth sorry is um just a country which internationally if someone's from the UK
probably we can find out where in the UK they're from the records are centralised so all the birth
marriages and death records are centralised at the general register office. Internationally,
primarily records are held more locally. So unless you know which region of a country someone's come
from, then you really don't know how to get under the skin of the research to begin with. So a lot
of what we do in the international team is going a step backwards and trying to find out a lot
more about the deceased person. So we're making inquiries around the person that's passed away to
try and build up a story of their life. Why did they end up in a particular country that they're
in? Do they have family members that are aware of the case? Maybe they just migrated on their
own for economic reasons. Um, you know, did they own a business here where we can try and speak to
the old company directors? Is there any passenger lists which will show where they came from? Um,
and then again, like you have to go over everything with a fine tooth comb because even
on a passenger list or a naturalisation, someone may have put they're from the port that they
disembarked from or they may just put the closest city to where they're from. So really it's kind of
in international at least finding beneficiaries in the first place is a massive hurdle and then once
you get to speak to the beneficiaries then again it's kind of convincing them that we're legitimate
and kind of taking them through the whole process. A lot of people are unfamiliar with the work that
we do in the UK at least. We were on a TV show for 5 years on the BBC called Heir Hunters. So then
we're in prime position at that time because we'd be doing the research into the family trees whilst
ringing people and they'll be like I'm watching you on the TV right now. So the level of doubt was
removed but the further we get away from the TV TV show being on it does get a bit more difficult.
But Finders is is quite proactive in staying quite head above the parapet in terms of media making
sure we're exposed and making sure people know we exist. So So you basically you've got someone
who's who's passed away. they've left assets anywhere in the world. Um you will try you'll try
and try and trace those heirs but also at the same time um you'll be be looking for those assets. Um
so presumably you know when when we get contacted by clients who whose whose um relatives passed
away we carry out land searches, company searches uh etc. And those are those kind of similar
searches you'd be carrying out as well when you're looking for those assets and financial assets and
and properties. We would do on a lot of UK cases. We have an in-house team that looks at missing
assets. So obviously um you know especially when Finders is working on a commission basis. It's
within everyone's best interests to increase the value of the estate. But it is a standalone
service that we offer to solicitors even if we're working on a fee basis. But that would be a very
much UK specific asset search. Internationally looking for assets. There are some countries that
we really can't do any investigation in in terms of assets. Um, Spain through yourselves is one
of the countries luckily where we do have uh the ability to have a look around for assets. But we
get I probably get an inquiry once every other day from a law firm in the UK where they want to do a
global sweep of assets because someone had some assets overseas or someone had some assets in a
particular country and then it becomes a lot more difficult. It is literally the cliche of looking
for a needle in the hay stack. So unless they have some documentary evidence that some assets
existed, in which instance it may go through our international asset specialist team where they can
actually recover and kind of reconstitute assets from overseas into a UK estate by um taking out
grants or receing grants and that kind of thing. But it's very different from looking for assets.
But if assets come to our attention across the course of the investigation, I think Sophie's
got at least one in the case at the minute where it seems like Sophie, I don't know,
property in Nigeria keeps coming up every day on one particular case. We would always investigate
it. But and and what what comes first, Ryan? Does the the heir come first or does the property come
first? I mean, how does it get to you? I mean, any notification that someone's passed away
comes to us first. So that could be in all the various methods that I um explained earlier. But
also we are conscious especially if Finders is going to conduct the work speculatively. We are
conscious of knowing that there's an asset. Also we don't want to be disturbing people
if if they're going to you know if the estate's going to be insolvent at the end of the day. Um,
primarily real estate is a good asset to start with, but across the board at Finders, we'll do
everything from pro bono work to 5,000, 10,000, £3 million, you know, anything in between. So,
as long as there's someone that's passed away and there's an asset to be distributed or if it's the
pro bono work for the local authorities, then we will take a look at it. Um and then you know the
gene energy comes in the locating the family and then there's a supplementary work like you said
then we'll start looking for additional assets and looking for a will. It's an interesting thing
where it is kind of cart before the horse sometimes because often across the board at
Finders we're locating beneficiaries but then we need to find someone within the family that then
has the authority to instruct a law firm that then can ask someone to go into the property and look
for a will and then there might be a will to the dog shelter or the cat's home or something like
that and then we have to let everybody down that we've located but often people are quite happy
that the last will in testament has been honoured so sometimes cases fall away like that. Yeah,
that's that's interesting because in the I mean in the UK we've got a wills register just like
we have in Spain, but here it's it's a bit more a bit more thorough in that most Spanish wills
are signed in front of a notary and the notary here will hold on to the signed copy and then let
the civil registry know. So along with the death certificate, once we've got a death certificate,
we'll know quite quickly whether or not there was a there's a Spanish will signed by that person.
Um, and of course if someone if you thought the heir was someone who might be on that will and it
turns out that they're not then then the notary won't release that a copy of that will. So then
you've got to go look and they don't usually help you and say all right um you know Mrs. Smith is
not on Mr. Smith's in his will but then they won't then say oh but someone else is and they won't say
who that is. So, so that that's that's where you guys come in and play a crucial crucial part. But,
um, finding out about what the deceased was up to, what he was doing or she was doing, their
whereabouts before dying and and the how they, you know, managed their lives. That's probably,
you know, that's an important process, isn't it? Yeah. And you hit the nail on the head of
something I kind of missed to say earlier in terms of um hurdles that we face is access to records.
And as you said, there is a probate registry here in the UK where if a probate has been granted,
it's public record and we can look at that probate and we can at least see who the administrator is

Complete class name: Finding Wills in England and Wales Online, Part 3: Ecclesiastical Probate Courts, pre-1858 – Vivien Brown (24 Mar 2024)

Vivien Brown explains the Lower Ecclesiastical Courts at a more local level and what records might be available through them. She carefully explains what might be found in probate records and wills that will be useful in family history research. She also demonstrates different way to find these records.

For more information: https://familyhistory.lib.byu.edu/virtual-classes/finding-wills-in-england-and-wales-online-part-3-ecclesiastical-probate-courts-pre-1858

Slide Deck and Class Links: https://familyhistory.lib.byu.edu/virtual-classes/finding-wills-in-england-and-wales-online-part-3-ecclesiastical-probate-courts-pre-1858

metadata.title: Analyzing Probate Records: Finding Our Ancestor's Stories
metadata.author: FamilySearch
metadata.shortDescription:
Probate Records can shed light on your ancestor's stories even when there's no will left behind. Learn how to use these records to find clues and help answer your family history research questions.

In this video, we learn about two types of probate records: testate and intestate. By analyzing probate records, we receive vital clues for finding our ancestor's stories. Probate records may be the key to unlocking exciting family stories telling of drama, sacrifice, service, day-to-day life,  and more!

This presentation was part of RootsTech Connect 2021. Find hundreds of free family history classes, keynotes, and more. http://familysearch.me/RootsTech 

#rootstechconnect 

RootsTech is hosted by FamilySearch, a global nonprofit organization dedicated to creating inspiring family discovery experiences. RootsTech is the premier global event and learning resource for making family connections and receiving guidance to help people learn more about their families.  
 
FamilySearch is an international, nonprofit organization dedicated to helping people all over the world connect with their family: past, present, and future. Our partnerships with thousands of record custodians and major genealogical organizations allow us to make billions of records available for you to research your family tree free of charge! Regardless of where or how you research your ancestry, we have specialists all over the world to help you experience the joy of connecting with your heritage.

metadata.shortDescription:
Probate records are, arguably, the single most valuable genealogical records for pre-1880 U.S. family history research. Join Crista Cowan for a look at how these records are organized on Ancestry and how best to search them.

Start Your Journey Today:
http://www.ancestry.com/s89386/t38352/rd.ashx

Subscribe: http://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsc0AQkAh_2cQmxqwD6VWRw?sub_confirmation=1

About Ancestry:
Bringing together science and self-discovery, Ancestry helps everyone, everywhere discover the story of what led to them. Our sophisticated engineering and technology harnesses family history and consumer genomics, combining billions of rich historical records and millions of family trees to over 10 million and counting to provide people with deeply meaningful insights about who they are and where they come from. 
We’ve pioneered and defined this category, developing new innovations and technologies that have reinvented how people make family history discoveries. And these discoveries can give everyone a greater sense of identity, relatedness, and their place in the world.

Connect with Ancestry:
Visit Ancestry’s Official Site: https://www.ancestry.com/
Like Ancestry on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Ancestry/
Follow Ancestry on Twitter: https://twitter.com/Ancestry
Follow Ancestry on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ancestry

Getting Started With Probate Records | Ancestry
https://www.youtube.com/user/AncestryCom

metadata.title: How to Find Wills and Probate Records for Free and What They Can Tell Us
metadata.author: Ancestry Aimee
metadata.shortDescription:
Probate records are more than wills! These records are crucial in family history research when working to discover your ancestry pre-1850. Instagram: ancestrybyaimee Facebook: @aimeecross2

Genealogy research, particularly in the 1700’s and early 1800’s, is more difficult. We rely on different record types and one of the best is wills and other probate records. Many feel if there is no will, no luck; but don’t miss important ancestor hints when you can’t find a will – there can be lots of other records.

Here we talk about what other records may be included in a probate and how to conduct a probate court records search with FamilySearch (FREE) and Ancestry ($) being my favorites! 

Pre-1850’s Strategies with Connie Knox of GenealogyTV https://youtu.be/VWma15_Lc3M

My video of Deed Records https://youtu.be/X8NNeexlV8E

Pre-1850’s Strategies Playlist 

Judy Russell’s Article – Consideration of $1 https://www.legalgenealogist.com/2013/08/01/a-matter-of-consideration/

Ancestry Will and Probate Database  https://www.ancestry.com/search/categories/36/

Find me at https://ancestryaimee.com

0:00 Intro
0:30 Pre-1850 Strategies with Genealogy TV
1:10 What are probate records?
1:30 Probate 101
2:05 Laws affecting probate – Common Law v. Civil Law, Dowry and Guardianships
4:12 Information wills can provide
6:45 Will provides daughter’s married names and indicates which of his two wives had which children
10:04 Letter of Administration names wife
10:31 Will destroyed but information found in newspaper
11:57 Estate notices
12:24 Where to find probate records
13:45 Ancestry.com
16:10 FamilySearch
21:02 Wrap Up  
#FamilyHistory #Genealogy #Ancestry #GenealogyTV #ProbateResearch

Music "Something Elated" by Broke for Free. 
https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Broke_For_Free/Something_EP/Broke_For_Free_-_Something_EP_-_05_Something_Elated
Aimee Cross, a professional genealogist based in the United States, shares practical, step-by-step strategies. On Ancestry Aimee we break down brick walls, use records correctly, organize family history research, build accurate, well-sourced family trees, all while avoiding common genealogy mistakes. Terrific for beginner and intermediate researchers who want real progress, not just hints. 

Be sure to catch reviews of the latest Ancestry, FamilySearch, MyHeritage, Find A Grave, and other genealogy platform features, essential for your family search. 

Aimee's goal is to make genealogy feel approachable, logical, and rewarding—so you can trust the discoveries you make.

👉 New videos and research guidance to help you build your family tree with confidence.

metadata.shortDescription:
Learn more about how to get the most out of probate records. This session, Records Analysis: Level up Your Probate Skills, will also cover substitute records that can be used to find similar genealogical information.

This presentation was part of RootsTech Connect 2021. Find hundreds of free family history classes, keynotes, and more. http://familysearch.me/RootsTech 

#rootstechconnect

RootsTech is hosted by FamilySearch, a global nonprofit organization dedicated to creating inspiring family discovery experiences. RootsTech is the premier global event and learning resource for making family connections and receiving guidance to help people learn more about their families.  

FamilySearch is an international, nonprofit organization dedicated to helping people all over the world connect with their family: past, present, and future. Our partnerships with thousands of record custodians and major genealogical organizations allow us to make billions of records available for you to research your family tree free of charge! Regardless of where or how you research your ancestry, we have specialists all over the world to help you experience the joy of connecting with your heritage.

metadata.shortDescription:
Probate records can help genealogists scale that brick wall between generations and add information about their family. If your ancestor had assets, they probably had probate papers. This class follows the estate from the documents to the final settlement. It also covers items such as dower rights. It does not offer legal advice. 

This program was created for an adult audience. 

Please be sure to like and share! Visit our website to register for upcoming in-person and virtual Genealogy programming events! https://www.mymcpl.org/genealogy 

Check more Genealogy virtual programming videos on our playlist here: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLnm7vznxHH_cDXKlVbtZtZ3et2etxoLne

metadata.title: Understanding Wills, Probate, Estate Records, and Women's Rights for Genealogy
metadata.author: Genealogy TV
metadata.shortDescription:
Wills, probate and estate records can be the best family history records you ever find. Additionally, understanding your female ancestors rights with regard to land ownership, dower rights, and their place in society at the time, can help you know how to find women in the records to help with your family tree.  

In this episode, we explore what to look for in wills, estates, understanding probate, land, vital records, civil law vs. common law states and tying the records together. 

Learn the definitions of the language used in legal documents. Learn where to find women prior to the 1850 census, when women and children were not named in the census records. Guest Judy Russell, The Legal Genealogist, explains it all.

metadata.title: Using Land and Probate Records in Family History Research Laurie Bradshaw
metadata.author: Gary Foster
metadata.shortDescription:
Join with Laurie Bradshaw, an experienced genealogist in this Mesa FamilySearch Library webcast.

Learn what Land and Probate records to research your ancestors and learn more about the origin of their surname, where they lived, and how they lived.

Begin your journey to learn who you are and the opportunities you now have because of the real experiences they had to endure for your freedoms.

Laurie recorded this video in front of a live audience in Mesa, Arizona in 2016, and shares this recording with you hoping you will learn the basic tools to assist you in your research.

Laurie is an experienced researcher and this video will assist you in your family history research.

metadata.title: What Happens After Death: Finding and Using Probate Records
metadata.author: Allen County Public Library
metadata.shortDescription:
Wills and probate records can offer a wealth of information for family historians, but finding your ancestor in these court records and deciphering historic legal jargon can be challenging. Join practicing attorney David Singleton for an introduction to using probate records in your research!

*Please note that there will be no legal advice given during this talk. The purpose of this presentation is solely to provide historical context as well as a general understanding of legal terms.

David Singleton is an associate attorney in Fort Wayne, Indiana with Blackburn Romey. He graduated with highest honors from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. David has been recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers®, a division of Thomson Reuters®, and has been named one of the Top 40 Under 40 civil plaintiff attorneys by the National Trial Lawyers organization. David conducts motion and appellate practice for Blackburn Romey’s Fort Wayne and South Bend offices and also handles case files in litigation. He has successfully argued on behalf of clients before numerous Indiana trial courts and the Indiana Court of Appeals. David is admitted to practice law before all Indiana state courts, the United States District Courts for Indiana’s Northern and Southern Districts, and the Supreme Court of the United States. https://www.blackburnromey.com/

Handout: https://static.libnet.info/frontend-images/pdfs/acpl/Genealogy/Handout_What_Happens_After_Death_Finding_and_Using_Probate_Records.pdf

metadata.title: What’s in a Probate Record and How to Use it for Genealogical Research– James Tanner (10 Sep 2023)
metadata.author: BYU Library Family History Center
metadata.shortDescription:
Probate records are some of the most valuable historical records for genealogical research. This class covers some of the basics of research using probate records. It is possible to use probate records to find some most difficult historical information such as women's maiden names, missing children, difficult or unusual family relationships and other equally puzzling problems. Take some time to learn some of the basics and begin to use probate records.
For more information: https://familyhistory.lib.byu.edu/virtual-classes/whats-in-a-probate-record-and-how-to-use-it-for-genealogical-research

metadata.title: Digging Deep into Death Records - James Tanner
metadata.author: BYU Library Family History Center
metadata.shortDescription:
There are many resources for finding and using death records. James give a great overview of where you can look for death records and how there are documents that are valuable that you wouldn't typically think of as a great resource.
For more information: https://familyhistory.lib.byu.edu/all-webinars/digging-deep-into-death-records

metadata.shortDescription:
It's easy to find an entry in the Social Security Death Index. But have you uncovered the "Last Benefit/Last Resident" clues?

Start Your Journey Today:
http://www.ancestry.com/s89715/t38352/rd.ashx

Subscribe: http://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsc0AQkAh_2cQmxqwD6VWRw?sub_confirmation=1

About Ancestry:
Bringing together science and self-discovery, Ancestry helps everyone, everywhere discover the story of what led to them. Our sophisticated engineering and technology harnesses family history and consumer genomics, combining billions of rich historical records and millions of family trees to over 10 million and counting to provide people with deeply meaningful insights about who they are and where they come from. 
We’ve pioneered and defined this category, developing new innovations and technologies that have reinvented how people make family history discoveries. And these discoveries can give everyone a greater sense of identity, relatedness, and their place in the world.

Part of our continuing sourcing series, Ancestry Anne walks you through how to source vital records from Ancestry.com and elsewhere.

Subscribe: http://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsc0AQkAh_2cQmxqwD6VWRw?sub_confirmation=1

About Ancestry:
Bringing together science and self-discovery, Ancestry helps everyone, everywhere discover the story of what led to them. Our sophisticated engineering and technology harnesses family history and consumer genomics, combining billions of rich historical records and millions of family trees to over 10 million and counting to provide people with deeply meaningful insights about who they are and where they come from. 
We’ve pioneered and defined this category, developing new innovations and technologies that have reinvented how people make family history discoveries. And these discoveries can give everyone a greater sense of identity, relatedness, and their place in the world.

metadata.title: What death records are you missing?
metadata.author: Ancestry Aimee
metadata.shortDescription:
Have you overlooked available death records to find out more about your ancestors? Or are you trying to determine someone's date and place of death? This video gives various sources of death information, many which are often overlooked in your genealogy research. 

👩🏻✈️ Join the Aimee's Crew for PERKS -- a special monthly livestream and free handouts: https://tinyurl.com/AimeesCrew

🌟 NEEED HELP? Zoom coaching available starting at $35.  Visit https://ancestryaimee.com for more information! 

❤️  Your support makes these videos possible! Support the channel for $2 a month. Thanks! ☕️ (https://www.patreon.com/aimeecross) 

👉To see my favorites: https://www.amazon.com/shop/aimeecross-genealogyhints

🙋♀️ Find me at https://ancestryaimee.com
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ancestryaimee/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/aimeecross2  

#familyhistory #genealogy #ancestry #familysearch

Intro music: "Something Elated" by Broke for Free. https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Broke_For_Free/Something_EP/Broke_For_Free_-_Something_EP_-_05_Something_Elated
Aimee Cross, a professional genealogist based in the United States, shares practical, step-by-step strategies. On Ancestry Aimee we break down brick walls, use records correctly, organize family history research, build accurate, well-sourced family trees, all while avoiding common genealogy mistakes. Terrific for beginner and intermediate researchers who want real progress, not just hints. 

Be sure to catch reviews of the latest Ancestry, FamilySearch, MyHeritage, Find A Grave, and other genealogy platform features, essential for your family search. 

Aimee's goal is to make genealogy feel approachable, logical, and rewarding—so you can trust the discoveries you make.

👉 New videos and research guidance to help you build your family tree with confidence.

metadata.title: What They Found in a Retired Postal Worker's Flat | Heir Hunters S11 Ep7
metadata.author: Heir Hunters
metadata.shortDescription:
A visit to a retired postal worker's flat leads the heir hunters to a valuable discovery.

The search for the family of a much-liked man from Tooting, south London, reveals he was descended from one of Britain's early tobacco merchants. Meanwhile, a visit to the home of a retired post office worker leads the team to a valuable discovery, and a fresh hunt for the people entitled to it.

Heir Hunters follows the probate researchers racing to trace the rightful heirs to unclaimed estates, before the money passes to the Crown as bona vacantia. Full episode: Season 11, Episode 7. First shown on BBC One in 2017.

Could you be a missing heir? Tell us your family's story in the comments.

▶ Subscribe for new full episodes every week
▶ Watch every Season 11 episode in the playlist

#HeirHunters #UnclaimedFortune #FamilyHistory #MissingHeir #Inheritance #UnclaimedEstates #Genealogy #FamilySecrets #Ancestry #BonaVacantia #RealStories #BBCDocumentary #UKDocumentary

How to find family members of a deceased person is one of the biggest challenges in probate, surplus funds, and unclaimed money cases. In this video, I share 6 proven ways to locate heirs and next of kin so you can move cases forward and close deals.

Join our great community: skool.com/surplusinstitute 

Whether you’re working probate cases, surplus funds, mortgage overages, or unclaimed property, knowing how to find family members of a deceased owner is critical if you want to close deals and help families recover money that’s rightfully theirs.

In this 6-minute training, you’ll learn:

How to find next of kin when the owner is deceased

Where to search for family members and heirs

How to use public records, probate filings, and obituaries

What to do when there is no will or obvious relatives

How professionals locate heirs legally and ethically

Common mistakes that cause people to miss family members

This is the exact process I use in real surplus and probate cases, and it works whether you’re brand new or already closing deals.

If you’re serious about building a business around surplus funds, probate leads, or unclaimed money, this is foundational knowledge you can’t skip.

👉 Subscribe for more real-world training on surplus funds, probate, and unclaimed property

👉 Share this video with anyone working probate or estate cases

metadata.title: Declaration Under Probate Code 13101 Tutorial
metadata.author: California State Controller's Office

segments.text: Welcome to this tutorial on how to complete the Declaration Under Probate Code Section
13101 Form located on the California State Controller's
Unclaimed Property Website.
To navigate to the Declaration Under Probate form from the State Controller's Office website,
click on Unclaimed Property.
Next, click the link for Claim Filing Instructions and Forms.
Lastly, scroll down to the bottom of the page, and click the link for
the Declaration Under Probate Code 13101 form.
The Declaration Under Probate Form is used for Heir claims, as a way to declare that
no Probate was required for an estate, or that the Administrator
or Personal Representative of the estate has provided
consent in writing stating the claimant is entitled to the Unclaimed Property.
At the top of the form, fill in the name, location, and date of passing for the deceased
owner.
This information can be found on the deceased owner's death certificate.
In section 3, check one of the following appropriate boxes:
Check the first box if there are no court proceedings pending, nor been conducted to
administer the decedent's estate in California, and that
no personal representative or special administrator has been
appointed by the court to administer the estate.
Check the second box if there is written consent from the decedent's personal representative
providing for you to receive payment, transfer or delivery
of the properties listed in Section 5.
In section 5, list all of the Property ID Numbers you are claiming.
You may attach a separate sheet if there are too many properties to list on the form.
In that case, simply write *see attached list*.
Please note that your Claim ID Number is not acceptable in this section, only the Property
ID Numbers that are part of your claim.
In section 6, check one of the following appropriate boxes:
Check the first box if the claimant is a beneficiary listed in the decedent's will; or, if the
decedent did not leave a will, but the claimant is a direct
relative of the decedent, such as a spouse, child, grandchild,
parent, and so on.
Check the second box if the claimant is the guardian or conservator of the estate of the
person entitled to any of the decedent's property.
Or if the claimant is the trustee of the decedent's trust, the personal representative of a beneficiary
of the decedent's estate, or is an attorney-in-fact
as part of a legally executed Durable Power of Attorney
for the claimant.
Fill in the name of the person or the name of the trust entitled to the decedent's
property, whichever is applicable.
Finally, the claimant's signature, printed name, and date the claimant makes this declaration
is required at the bottom of the form.
By signing this form, you declare the statements made on this form are true under penalty of
perjury.
A notary is not required on this form.
If you have any questions, please contact the State Controller's Office by phone at
Our Call Center is available 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pacific Time, Monday through Friday, excluding
state holidays.
The California State Controller's team is committed to helping rightful owners receive
their property.
Please help spread the word by sharing this tutorial with family and friends who may have
unclaimed property waiting for them.

metadata.title: Table of Heirship Tutorial
metadata.author: California State Controller's Office

segments.text: Welcome to this tutorial on how to complete the Table of Heirship Form located on the
California State Controller's Unclaimed Property Website.
To navigate to the Table of Heirship form from the State Controller's Office website,
click on Unclaimed Property.
Next, click the link for Claim Filing Instructions and Forms.
Lastly, scroll down to the bottom of the page, and click the link for the Table
of Heirship form.
The Table of Heirship Form is used for Heir claims, where the owner passed intestate,
with no Will, Trust, or other Estate Plan, and Probate was
not required.
This form provides detail about the family of the deceased owner, to determine how any
funds that belonged to the owner should be distributed.
At the top of the form, above Section 1, list the name of the deceased owner.
Next, list the date of their passing.
Just below that, list the property ID number you are claiming.
If there are multiple Property ID Numbers, list one of the Property ID Numbers.
These can be found on your claim form, or on the property details screen on the Unclaimed
Property website.
In section 1, list the name of the spouse of the deceased owner, or none, if they were
never married.
If the deceased owner had more than one spouse, list the names in chronological order, and
be sure to include the year the marriage occurred.
If the owner was divorced at the time of death, write *divorced* next to the spouse's
name.
Next, list the birthdate and date of death for the spouse if known.
In section 2, list all of the deceased owner's children, whether they are living or deceased.
If the owner did not have any children, write *none* in this field.
Be sure to list the name of each child's parent from section one under Parent's Name.
Next, list the birthdate and date of death for each child, if known.
In section 3, list all of the grandchildren of the deceased owner, whether living or deceased.
Be sure to include their parent's name in this section under Parent's Name.
Next, list the birthdate and date of death for each grandchild, if known.
Section 4 list the name of the parents of the deceased owner, including their date of
birth and their date of death, if applicable.
In section 5 you will list the names of all siblings of the deceased owner, whether they
are living or deceased.
Next, list the birthdate and date of death for each sibling, if known.
If the owner did not have any siblings, write *none*.
In section 6, list the nieces and nephews of the deceased owner, whether living or deceased.
Next, list the birthdate and date of death for each niece or nephew, if known.
If the owner did not have any nieces or nephews, write *none*.
For any of the previous sections on the Table of Heirship, if there is not enough room to
list everyone you need to in any section, you can attach
a second Table of Heirship Form to add the additional names.
At the bottom of the form, print your name in the first box, and sign in the second box.
In signing this form, you declare the information provided on this form is true under penalty
of perjury.
A notary is not required on this form.
If you have any questions, please contact the State Controller's Office by phone at
Our Call Center is available 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pacific Time, Monday through Friday, excluding
state holidays.
The California State Controller's team is committed to helping rightful owners receive
their property.
Please help spread the word by sharing this tutorial with family and friends who may have
unclaimed property waiting for them.

metadata.author: Heir Hunters
metadata.shortDescription:
Inside the walls of one of the world's most prestigious universities — a family of servants. Across the Atlantic — the luxury liners that carried a generation into a new world.

Research into two family trees uncovers the hidden history of domestic service inside one of the world's most prestigious universities, where generations quietly kept the institution running. A second case reveals how the golden age of luxury transatlantic steam liners helped change the course of 20th-century history — and the lives of one family in particular.

Could you be an heir to an unclaimed estate? Follow the race to find missing relatives before the Treasury takes the lot.

▶ Subscribe for full episodes of Heir Hunters
▶ Watch the full Season 9 playlist

#HeirHunters #Inheritance #UnclaimedEstates #FamilyHistory #Genealogy #BonaVacantia #MissingHeirs #ProbateResearch #RealStories #BBCDocumentary #FamilySecrets #UKDocumentary

 A recovery agent, also known as an property investigator or heir finder, is a professional or a company that specializes in helping individuals or entities locate and recover unclaimed funds or property. These agents play a critical role in reuniting rightful owners with their unclaimed assets, often for a fee or a percentage of the recovered amount. Here's a detailed overview of how the process works
 
1.) Research and Identification:
 Data Analysis: Unclaimed Property Investigators use various databases, both public and private, to identify unclaimed property that belongs to individuals or businesses. They may access state unclaimed property databases, court records and other sources of information.

- Matching:
  They match the unclaimed property data with potential owners using identifiers like names, addresses and other personal information.

2.) Contacting Potential Claimants:
Skip Trace/ Outreach: 
 Once a match is identified, Unclaimed Property Investigators contact the potential claimants through mail, phone calls, or emails. They inform the claimants about the existence of unclaimed funds or property and offer their services to assist in the recovery process.

3.) Verification and Documentation:
 Verification: 
 Unclaimed Property Investigators help claimants verify their identity and their right to the unclaimed property. This may involve gathering necessary documents such as identification, proof of address, legal documents  any other relevant records.

 Filing Claims: 
 They assist in preparing and submitting the required forms and documentation to the appropriate state unclaimed property office.

4.)Compensation
 Contingency Fees: 
 Unclaimed Property Investigators work on a contingency fee basis, meaning they only get paid if they successfully recover the unclaimed funds for the claimant. #OhioUnclaimedFunds #UnclaimedFunds #DivisionUnclaimedFunds

This video is a replay of a live webinar recorded on February 28, 2024 hosted by the Better Business Bureau of Central Ohio where we covered everything on claiming your unclaimed funds.
Unclaimed Funds is lost or forgotten money from inactive accounts that is reported by banks and businesses to the State of Ohio Division of Unclaimed Funds for safekeeping. The money come from inactive checking accounts, savings accounts, refund/credit balances, uncashed cashier’s checks, life insurance benefits, stocks & bonds, and safe deposit box contents. After attending this webinar, you will learn: What are unclaimed funds, how to find out if you have any, and the steps to claiming funds, Claiming on behalf of a deceased family member and the required documentation,  Claims timeline and delays, Claims status, and Claims resources. Visit unclaimedfunds.ohio.gov to search your name and claim your money today!

metadata.title: Ohio Unclaimed Funds: How to Claim Your Cash in 3 Steps (HB 96 Deadline Explained) Webinar 2-5-2026
metadata.author: ohiocommerce
metadata.shortDescription:
There’s nearly $5 billion in unclaimed money owed to Ohioans—and some of it could be yours. In this step by step webinar, the Ohio Department of Commerce Division of Unclaimed Funds teams up with the Better Business Bureau (BBB) and America250 Ohio to show you exactly how to search, file, and get paid—safely. 

What you’ll learn
• 3 easy steps to claim: Search your name, review required documents, and upload everything online—no fee, no middleman. (Covered in the webinar.)
• Identity & address verification done right: what documents to submit and how to avoid delays. (Covered in the webinar.)
• New online system benefits: faster approvals for many smaller claims and a self service portal to upload documents and check claim status. 
• Deadline alert (HB 96): Starting January 1, 2026, you have 10 years to claim funds from the date they were reported—or you lose the ability to claim them. Act now. 
• Fraud proofing your claim: Use BBB Scam Tracker to verify offers and spot scams before you engage. 

Start here (official links)
• Search & file your claim (free): unclaimedfunds.ohio.gov/app/claim-funds 
• Upload your claim documents & check status: unclaimedfunds.ohio.gov 
• BBB Scam Tracker (look up/report scams): bbb.org/scamtracker 
• America250 Ohio (learn more): america250-ohio.org 

Need help?
• Email: claims@com.ohio.gov 
• Phone: (614) 466 4433 

Important: Due to high claim volume, some claims may take longer than the expected 120 days. Submitting complete, correct documents is the fastest way to get paid. 

Chapters (timestamps)
0:00 – Welcome & why this matters (America250 Ohio)
2:03 – BBB: How to spot scams + Scam Tracker
4:54 – Unclaimed Funds 101: what counts, where money comes from (bank accounts, life insurance, dividends)
11:05 – High volume & staffing: what that means for your timeline
19:18 – Required documents: ID, SSN verification, proof of address, W 9
23:02 – Live walk through: filing a claim online
25:23 – Contact & next steps

Key takeaways & tips
• Use your current email and full SSN when filing—many properties are matched by SSN. (Covered in the webinar.)
• Don’t narrow your search by city/ZIP unless your name is very common; broader searches often find more properties. (Covered in the webinar.)
• Notary is only required if your total claim amount exceeds $3,000. (Covered in the webinar.)
• If you’re claiming for a deceased loved one, gather probate documents first, then file online. (Covered in the webinar.)

Why now?
Ohioans reclaimed $111M in 2025 after the Division launched its improved online system—and this year’s goal is even bigger. Don’t wait. Search, file, and get your money back. 
#UnclaimedMoney #Ohio #ConsumerProtection #BBB #America250Ohio #OhioCommerce #ClaimYourFunds

metadata.title: What Documentation is Needed for Unclaimed Funds
metadata.author: ohiocommerce
metadata.shortDescription: Ohio Department of Commerce’s Division of Unclaimed Funds Claims Examiner, Supervisor Anitra Davis, answers frequently asked questions about the required documentation that is needed and why it's important to claim your funds.  She discusses everything from social security numbers to what is needed to show proof of address to claim on behalf of a deceased person and the timeline for processing claims. Visit unclaimedfunds.ohio.gov to search and see if you have unclaimed funds today! #divisionunclaimedfunds  #ohiocommerce #ohiounclaimedfunds #unclaimedfunds

metadata.shortDescription: The San Luis Obispo County Clerk-Recorder's Office created a 3-minute video to walk viewers through the process of searching for property title documentation online

segments.text: The County of San Luis Obispo
Clerk-Recorder's Office serves a number
of important functions on behalf of
local residents. One of these functions
is recording and maintaining records of
land ownership within the county. The
recorder's official records provide
public access to information regarding
land and land ownership. Recent media
stories regarding fraud scams have led
to some property owners wanting to check
on the status of their recorded title.
We'd like to take a few minutes to walk
you through exactly how to do this
online.
The Clerk-Recorder's website can be
reached at slovote.com.
The simplest way to access the document
search function is by clicking on this
graphic depicting books, which says
begin your recorded document search.
That will take you to this official
record search portal.
One way to conduct a title search is by
clicking the top button, which says name
search.
From there, you can enter the property
owner's name, but be sure to follow the
format of last name, then first name
with no comma, then click search. Keep
in mind, the more information you
include here, the tighter the search
will be. So, don't include a middle name
or middle initial unless you're certain
that is in the original paperwork.
The search results will display in a
list like this. We've redacted the names
from this particular search because they
aren't important. What is important is
to now look for a recording entry that
says deed and is followed by
parentheses.

metadata.title: How I Actually Find Curative Title Leads
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke breaks down how she actually finds curative title leads and ownership problem opportunities in today’s Real Estate market.

Instead of chasing the same overcrowded lead lists as everyone else, Courtney explains why some of the best deals come from marketplace inefficiencies, abandoned processes, overlooked public records, and problems other investors simply do not know how to solve.

ATTENTION:
The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
Skip tracing makes or breaks curative title deals. If you can't find the owners, you can't close. Matt Hecker, co-founder of SmartSkip.io, runs a skip tracing platform and his own real estate investing business, so he sees both sides: the data and the dials.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Matt and Logan Fullmer break down how accurate skip tracing data really is, why you should track which phone numbers actually connect, and how SmartSkip layers multiple data providers to get better results. They also cover how to use relatives and associates to track down missing owners, the difference between regulated and unregulated data, and when to bulk dial vs. work a file by hand.

Plus, the cold caller's nightmare: a man who made about $65,000 a year as a side job suing investors who called him, and why knowing when to walk away from a 21-owner deal matters as much as knowing how to find them.

You'll learn:
- How accurate skip tracing data really is
- Why you should tag and track your phone numbers in your CRM
- How layering multiple data sources improves your hit rate
- How to use relatives and associates to find missing owners
- Regulated vs. unregulated data, and when you need each
- When to bulk dial and when to work leads one at a time
- How many owners is too many on a curative title deal

metadata.title: How to Get Your First Curative Title Deal: A Step-by-Step Guide
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
If you want to get your first curative title deal, you don't need the perfect list, expensive software, or to understand every complicated legal issue before you start.

You need to start developing the ability to recognize the problems other Real Estate investors overlook.

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke breaks down a practical, step-by-step process for finding and pursuing your first curative title opportunity.

Instead of starting with massive lists and trying to scale a strategy you don't understand yet, Courtney walks through how to pick a market, find distressed properties, research ownership and public records, identify potential title problems, narrow down the best opportunities, find the right people to contact, and start having conversations.

The goal isn't to become a title expert overnight. It's to start putting in the reps that teach you how to recognize where physical, financial, and ownership problems may be creating opportunities.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: How to Underwrite a Curative Title Deal (And Know When to Walk Away)
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
A property with a $210,000 ARV. A seller who originally thought she owned 50%. And now she's willing to sell her potential 25% interest for just $7,000.

Would you buy it?

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke walks through a real-world curative title lead and breaks down how she analyzes whether a messy ownership problem is actually worth solving.
Courtney breaks down how to build the fact pattern, separate facts from assumptions, determine what an ownership interest is actually worth, and work backward through the potential costs and risks standing between buying the interest and eventually getting paid.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

#probate #realestatecoaching #skiptracing Probate Data and Property Lookups: Live Real Estate Coaching for Probate Mastery students, hosted by @BillGrossProbate 

This week's training covered a ton of great topics with a heavy focus on skiptracing probate data and doing property lookups. Bill Gross and Probate Mastery students discuss how to find missing heirs for vacant property leads with a deceased owner. The group shares tips for probate real estate data production, using things like property lookups, forwarding addresses, and phone number lookups for probate court records. Bill Gross breaks down 4 different types of probate attorneys you can network with and how administration vs. litigation differ.  Other topics include how to approach probate property with a reverse mortgage, transferring title after death, and handling probate objections about commission.

Real Estate Coaching Q&A
0:00 Different Types of Probate Attorneys: Administration vs. Litigation (Probate Attorneys)
8:32 Vacant property with deceased owner: How to find missing heirs (Skiptracing)
11:50 Property lookups, forwarding address, and phone number lookups for probate court records (Probate Data)
17:52 Probate appraisal and estate inventory process (Probate Timeline)
22:13 How to approach probate leads with reverse mortgage and foreclosure situations (Probate Prospecting)
30:46 Deed after death: Do we have to open probate to transfer title in North Carolina? (Probate Process)
33:12 How to handle B2B objections about commissions vs. quality of work (B2B Networking)

Full probate podcast and show notes: https://probatemastery.com/ep67-probate-data-and-property-lookups

Join our Facebook Group, Estate Professionals Mastermind: https://facebook.com/groups/estateprofessionalsmastermind

Take the Probate Mastery Course and earn your Certified Probate Expert designation: https://probatemastery.com With our current promotional offer, you'll get access to live group coaching free!

metadata.title: How to Find Heirs for a Florida Probate Property
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
A property owner dies. No probate has been opened. You don't even know who the heirs are. Where do you start?

In this Messy Money micro episode, Florida probate attorney Al Nicoletti and I break down how Real Estate investors can start identifying the potential heirs and family members of a deceased property owner.

We discuss death certificates, obituaries, deeds, marriage and divorce records, and other public records that can help you start piecing together the ownership puzzle.

Watch the FULL Florida Probate Masterclass with Al Nicoletti: https://youtu.be/Dutmzc9gb30 

ATTENTION:
The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: Curative Title Research: How She Finds Missing Owners
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
When the owner of a property has died or disappeared, most investors walk away. Stephanie Shepherd has built her business on finding them. She's a title research specialist, California wholesaler, and joint venture partner for investors who get stuck on curative title deals.

Ten years ago, Stephanie was about to file for personal bankruptcy after a bad partnership in the surplus funds business. She started over, found a mentor, and taught herself title research through trial and error. Today investors bring her in at a forensic level: deeds from the 1800s, family trees six generations deep, name changes, adoptions, and streets that have been renamed since the original records were filed.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Stephanie and Logan Fullmer walk through exactly how she finds missing owners: why one-off skip tracing beats bulk, why she always searches the mailing address first, where data providers actually get their phone numbers, and what she says when she calls a family member so she doesn't sound like just another wholesaler.

You'll learn:
- Why one-off skip tracing gives you better data than bulk
- How to read a skip trace, and why the mailing address comes first
- Where skip tracing data really comes from
- What to say when you call a family member about a deceased owner
- How to build a family tree using Ancestry and old records
- When one house needs four probates, and when to walk away
- How she finds deals on California tax delinquent lists
- How adverse possession claims really work, and why most fail

TIMESTAMPS
0:00 Nearly bankrupt from a bad partnership
3:02 Why one-off skip tracing beats bulk
7:05 Always skip trace the mailing address first
15:00 What to say when you call the family
16:01 Building a family tree with Ancestry
23:02 When one house needs four probates
32:00 Finding deals on California tax delinquent lists
42:05 The North Carolina deed nobody could explain

#podcast #probate #realestateleads This is episode 85 of the Estate Professionals Mastermind Podcast. The episode type is Weekly Certified Probate Expert Mastermind.

In this episode, you will hear how to get probate leads from the courthouse, 3 probate success stories, and marketing tips and ideas to help you build a better probate business.

Hosted by Bill Gross of Probate Weekly.

Full Episode Notes and Links to Podcast Streams: https://probatemastery.com/get-probate-leads-from-courthouse

Take EARN (Earn Attorney Referrals Now): https://courses.magnumopusproject.com/earn

Bill Gross' Probate Cash Advance Series: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/get-probate-cash-tickets-411579925637
Canva Template for Probate Court Social Post: Available in the Probate Mastery Alumni group https://www.facebook.com/groups/ProbateMastery
EstateExec Guide, Reviews, and Interview with Dan Stickel: https://probatemastery.com/estateexec-probate-software-for-executors/ 
Free Guide to Probate for Investors: https://probatemastery.com/probate-for-investors-guide/


In this episode:
0:00 The probate niche and probate data vs. leads (Probate Niche)
3:29 How to get probate leads from the courthouse free. (Probate Business)
14:49 Easy, No-Face Social Media Post Template for probate court (Probate Marketing)
18:28 Katt Marketing Coach Reviews (Marketing Coaching)
21:38 Attorney Prospecting Ideas & Ancillary Probate Listing (Probate Success Story)
28:20 Bill's probate investing deal from a YouTube lead (Probate Success Story) 
30:03 Probate real estate referral systems and SOI marketing (Referral Marketing)

Congratulations to Bill for buying probate property, ClaireMonique for breaking out of her comfort zone, Deborah for getting a probate listing by providing value first, and Larry for hitting the pavement with his probate marketing plan.

Live participation is available for students of Chad Corbett's probate course. Enroll now: https://courses.magnumopusproject.com/checkout-page


Two major takeaways from this episode:

1) ClaireMonique wasn't able to get a probate list from All The Leads (They didn't have Pinal County leads), but she took action and ended up getting 5 years worth of probate records for free and now knows a lot more about her local probate court! Follow her footsteps!

2) Bill is generating his business without cold calling probates; If you're looking for a way to stop calling probate leads, focus on building your personal brand and attorney referral system through relationships and content.


“The value is the process, not the results"

Thank you to all the real estate agents and investors, attorneys, and financial services professionals who make these calls a great learning experience. Until next week - Happy learning!

metadata.title: Curative Title + Creative Finance: The Combo Most Investors Miss
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Most investors treat Curative title work and creative finance as two completely separate skill sets.

That is a mistake.

In this episode, Courtney Fricke and Ellis San Jose break down how combining Curative strategy with creative deal structuring can dramatically reduce risk, lower cash outlay, enhance returns, and create opportunities most investors never even see.

If you operate in messy estates, multiple-heir situations, liens, judgments, or stalled transactions, this conversation will expand your toolbox.

ATTENTION:
The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: How Wholesalers Can Turn Title Problems Into Profitable Curative Deals
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Real estate wholesalers are trained to find motivated sellers, negotiate the right price, and get deals closed. But what happens when a title or ownership problem gets in the way?

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke sits down with Stephen Keighery of Home Buyer Louisiana to discuss how an established wholesaling operation approaches curative title issues without trying to turn its acquisitions team into title experts.

Stephen explains why wholesalers don't necessarily need a dedicated curative title division—they need enough competency to recognize potentially solvable problems, determine whether the economics justify pursuing them, and know who to call when the problem exceeds their expertise. 


ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

And if you know an investor who could benefit from looking at complicated deals differently, share this episode with them.

metadata.title: Curative Title Explained: How Investors Make Money When Deals Can’t Close
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
In this first episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke sits down with Ellis San Jose, a 30+ year Real Estate investor who specializes in curative title work, the side of Real Estate most people avoid.

ATTENTION: The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

This conversation breaks down what curative title actually means in practical terms, why uninsurable properties often hide the biggest margins, and how experienced investors turn broken paperwork, ownership issues, and distressed documents into real profit. Instead of focusing on cosmetic rehabs and HGTV-style transformations, this episode looks at how value is created by solving problems on paper.

Courtney and Ellis also dig into why curative work pairs so well with creative strategies like seller financing and subject-to, how to evaluate whether a curative issue is solvable or a trap, and why time, risk analysis, and legal relationships matter more here than speed.

If you are interested in making money where other deals get stuck, this episode sets the foundation.

Topics covered in this episode:
- What curative title really means and why title insurance matters
- The difference between uninsurable and insurable property
- Why curative deals offer less competition and bigger safety margins
- How creative finance and curative strategies work together
- Common mistakes investors make when analyzing curative deals
- How to decide if the juice is worth the squeeze

metadata.title: Curative Title for Wholesalers: How He Turned a Dead Lead Into a Deal
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
What happens when three heirs own a property, but one of them can't be found?

For many real estate investors and wholesalers, that's where the deal dies.

But that was only one of the problems with this New Orleans property.
In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke sits down with Stephen Keighery of Home Buyer Louisiana to break down a real curative title deal his team recently closed.

Home Buyer Louisiana originally spoke with the family in 2021. Five years later, the situation looked very different. 

Instead of immediately writing it off as a dead lead, Steve's team kept asking a simple question:
Is there still an economically viable path to closing?

One of the biggest lessons from this case study is that you don't necessarily need to know the solution before pursuing the opportunity.

And sometimes that's the difference between a dead lead and a deal.
It's not always finding a more motivated seller. It's knowing what problem actually needs to be solved — and whether the economics justify solving it.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: How a Curative Title Investor Finds & Solves Deals Others Can't
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
What does curative title investing actually look like beyond buying partial interests from heirs?

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, I sit down with longtime curative real estate investor Karl Spielvogel to break down how he finds, researches, and solves messy real estate deals that other investors often overlook.

If you're a real estate investor, wholesaler, or agent interested in curative title, complicated ownership, distressed property, or the messy side of real estate, this conversation will give you a much broader look at what's possible.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

Connect with Karl Spielvogel: 
Text Karl: 70(four)-995-5385 — Best way to reach him by text
Business Line: 70(four)-777-7777 — Call and leave a message

TikTok: https://tiktok.com/@courtney.fricke

X: https://x.com/courtneyfricke
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@courtneyfricke
Website: www.CourtneyFricke.com

Join Curative Title Investing Facebook Group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/curativetitle 

Louisiana Real Estate Talks Podcast: https://www.youtube.com/@LouisianaRealEstateTalks 

Subscribe to the Messy Money Podcast for real-world conversations about combining curative title and creative finance to solve the messy problems that keep good real estate deals from getting done. And if you know an investor who could benefit from looking at complicated deals differently, share this episode with them.

metadata.title: 5 Curative Title Terms Every Investor Should Understand
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Most investors hear terms like quitclaim deed, cloud on title, and quiet title action but don't really understand what they mean. In this episode, I break down five of the most common curative title terms every investor should know and explain them in plain English.

What You'll Learn
-What fee simple ownership means
-How chain of title works
-What creates a cloud on title
-Why quitclaim deeds are misunderstood
-When a quiet title action may be necessary

CHAPTERS FOR THIS EPISODE:
00:00 Why Title Problems Kill Deals
01:12 What Is Fee Simple Title?
05:18 What Is Chain of Title?
10:47 What Is a Cloud on Title?
16:05 What Is a Quitclaim Deed?
21:37 What Is a Quiet Title Action?
28:10 Five Questions Every Investor Should Ask
31:22 Final Thoughts

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: How to Find Curative Title Deals Nobody Else Is Chasing
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
A lot of curative title investors are looking for the same thing: The secret list.

The problem is, if someone can hand you a copy-and-paste list of distressed properties, they can probably hand that exact same list to everyone else.

As more investors move into curative title, traditional lead sources like tax delinquency, code enforcement, probate, vacant properties, and foreclosure are only going to become more competitive.

So how do you find curative title opportunities other investors aren't chasing?

You learn how to build your own niche lists.

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Courtney Fricke breaks down what she means when she says she's made money in Real Estate simply by being curious—and shares a real curative title deal where one unusual creditor led her down a rabbit hole that ultimately uncovered an entirely new source of potential deals.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: Curative Title Explained by a Florida Probate Attorney
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
Curative title deals sound simple until you find out the heir who says she's the only sibling actually has 13 brothers and sisters. Al Nicoletti is a high-volume Florida probate attorney who has handled more than 2,000 probates, plus the quiet titles, partitions, and title problems that come with messy real estate deals.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Al and Logan Fullmer walk through how probate really works in curative title deals: why one property often needs two or three probates, the documents to gather before you ever call an attorney, the difference between summary and formal administration in Florida, and what happens when all you have is a copy of the will.

They also cover how creditors work in probate, when a partition lawsuit makes sense, how a quiet title can clear what a probate can't, and why you should get the title underwriter's sign-off before you file anything.

You'll learn:
- How to figure out who the real heirs are, and why people leave some out
- Why many curative title deals need more than one probate
- What documents to collect before you call a probate attorney
- The mistake most probate attorneys make on investor deals
- Summary vs. formal administration in Florida
- What happens when there's only a copy of the will
- When to use a partition lawsuit, and what it costs
- How quiet title actions clear title when probate isn't enough

0:00 "Just me"... then 13 more siblings
2:00 Why curative title deals need more than one probate
6:10 Documents to gather before calling a probate attorney
16:00 The mistake most probate attorneys make

40:02 An original will vs. a copy

metadata.title: The Probate Mistake New Real Estate Investors Make (Florida Attorney Case Study)
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
A newer Real Estate investor found what looked like a great probate opportunity.

There was just one problem. Actually, there were four.

Four separate probates needed to be opened to get the ownership cleaned up.

The investor hired Florida probate attorney Al Nicoletti, moved forward with the probate process, and then discovered something during the rest of their due diligence that killed the entire deal.

In this micro episode of the Messy Money Podcast, Al breaks down what went wrong and the expensive lesson every investor working probate and curative title deals should understand.

What You'll Learn:

-Why solving the probate problem isn't enough
-The due diligence mistake this investor made before opening probate
-Why probate and curative investors can get tunnel vision
-What investors should investigate before spending money curing an ownership problem
-How to avoid solving an expensive title problem on a deal you never should have pursued

Watch the FULL Florida Probate Masterclass with Al Nicoletti: https://youtu.be/Dutmzc9gb30

Check out this video series featuring USDA FSA staff speaking with experts on the topic of heirs’ property. These experts answer and address many of the common heirs’ property questions and concerns asked by heirs, as well as provide some best practices for when heirs are preparing to work with the resources provided through FSA.

Prior to the 2018 Farm Bill owners of heirs property could not qualify for USDA programs. However, thanks to the new provisions provided in the 2018 Farm Bill, heirs' property owners with farming and ranching operations can now utilize available resources provided by USDA FSA to secure a farm number and access USDA programs.

metadata.title: Heirs' Property with Jonathan Reynolds of Louisiana Appleseed
metadata.author: NOLA City Archives
metadata.shortDescription:
Have you inherited property? Do you plan to leave your home to your family?

Join Jonathan Reynolds of Louisiana Appleseed Public Interest Law Center in person or on Zoom to learn about heirs' property issues and the legal and Library resources that can help.

Learn about inherited property in this presentation by Louisiana Appleseed, a nonprofit organization dedicated to statewide policy, advocacy, and education. Louisiana Appleseed is focused on social justice, including issues related to title clearance, free legal help, and estate planning. Discover the ins and outs of heirs’ property and how to safeguard your heirs courtesy of attorney Jonathan Reynolds.

Jonathan Reynolds is a staff attorney for Louisiana Appleseed focusing on Heirs' Property. He earned a Bachelor of the Arts Degree from the University of New Orleans and a law degree from Loyola College of Law, New Orleans. Mr. Reynolds began his law career as a title examiner and abstractor for right-of-way and oil & gas projects. Prior to his legal career, while displaced from New Orleans due to Hurricane Katrina, Mr. Reynolds was a research assistant at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety. Mr. Reynolds is a native of New Orleans and long time member of the Bunny Friend Neighborhood Association.

This is a hybrid event with both virtual and in-person access--please excuse our boxes for the first 30 minutes!
