metadata.title: Heirs' Property 101
metadata.author: Center for Community Progress
metadata.shortDescription:
The first step of addressing widespread vacancy is identifying the types of vacant, abandoned, and deteriorated (VAD) properties that exist in the community. One of the more challenging property types to address is “heirs’ property.” Heirs’ property occurs when a property owner dies without a will, passing a property to multiple descendants, or heirs.

Addressing heirs’ property—also referred to as tangled title, family property, or family land—is complicated. Resolving tangled title requires tracking down all living heirs and specialized legal expertise. Some heirs may have no interest in caring for the property. Distant heirs may not even know they own a share. In the meantime, tangled title limits access to property maintenance resources. As a result, heirs’ properties can fall into serious disrepair and sit abandoned for decades, harming neighborhood stability.

In this webinar, the Center for Community Progress will discuss how these issues intersect with efforts to address VAD properties and how to address heirs’ property issues.

Join this webinar to:
• Learn why fractional, unrecorded ownership sets properties on the path to deterioration and abandonment
• Understand the tools that state and local governments have at their disposal to address vacant, abandoned, and deteriorated heirs’ property
• Hear examples of effective work that local governments and their community partners have done to address heirs’ property and maintain community stability

Speakers:
• Matt Kreis — General Counsel, Center for Community Progress

This webinar was a part of the Center for Community Progress' free lunch-and-learn webinar series. Webinars typically take place from 12:00–1:00 PM ET on the fourth Thursday of each month and cover range of topics from land banks and land banking to vacant land stewardship, strategic code enforcement, delinquent property tax enforcement, and more. 

View upcoming events: https://communityprogress.org/community-progress-webinars/
Subscribe to our newsletter: https://communityprogress.org/newsletter-signup/

metadata.title: Heirs' Property Training (Webinar from DBAN)
metadata.author: Farm Aid
metadata.shortDescription:
Annette Hiatt and Mary Henderson are senior staff attorneys with the Land Loss Prevention Project in North Carolina, where they provide direct legal services to farmers and landowners. In this training, they will discuss what heir property (or heirs' property) is, its historical context, how it affects farmers and other landowners, and how to assist folks who are dealing with it.

For more information, please visit https://farmaid.org/DBAN

Farm Aid's mission is to build a vibrant, family farm-centered system of agriculture in America. Farm Aid artists and board members Willie Nelson, Neil Young, John Mellencamp, Dave Matthews and Margo Price host an annual festival to raise funds to support Farm Aid's work with family farmers and to inspire people to choose family farm food. Since 1985, Farm Aid, with the support of the artists who contribute their performances each year, has raised more than $85 million to support programs that help farmers thrive, expand the reach of the Good Food Movement, take action to change the dominant system of industrial agriculture and promote food from family farms. 

______________________
This material is based upon work supported by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, under agreement number FSA24CPT0014425. Any opinions, findings, conclusions, or recommendations expressed in this publication are those of the author(s) and do not necessarily reflect the views of the U.S. Department of Agriculture. In addition, any reference to specific brands or types of products or services does not constitute or imply an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Agriculture for those products or services.

metadata.title: Preserving Homeownership: A Guide to Heirs Property for Housing Counselors
metadata.author: National Housing Resource Center
metadata.shortDescription:
This webinar focuses on the importance of heirs’ property and estate planning—key issues that can prevent families from keeping or passing down their homes. Without a clear title or estate plan in place, homeowners risk losing access to loss mitigation, FEMA assistance, and other essential resources.
 
The Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC) joined us for this webinar to highlight how housing counselors can help families understand the importance of estate planning, identify challenges related to heirs’ property early, and connect clients with trusted legal and community resources. We also heard from a housing counseling agency that is partnering with LISC, which has worked to put this work into practice.

metadata.title: Resolving Heirs' Property
metadata.author: MD Ag Law Education Initiative
metadata.shortDescription: This video covers steps to take to understand who legally owns the property, legal structures that can hold land owned by heirs' property owners, and tools and resources to assist.

The Uniform Law Commission, also known as the National Conference of Commissioners on Uniform State Laws, that commission worked to develop a model statute that states could adopt that would address partition laws.
and the Uniform Law Commission approved the Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act, or the UPHPA, in the summer of 2010.
So it's been with us a while.
It is important to note that the uniform law is not effective, however, in any state at all, unless or until some form of it is adopted by that state's legislature.
And this is a map actually of the states who have enacted the Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act.

metadata.author: Texas Probate Real Estate
metadata.shortDescription:
Probate attorney Nancy Perry Eaton (Law Office of Nancy Perry Eaton) and Jeremy Kritt explain Texas probate pitfalls: affidavits of heirship, AI errors and investor risks.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Introduction to Probate Real Estate
02:42 Understanding the Probate Process
05:11 Challenges with Affidavits of Heirship
07:42 The Role of Title Companies
10:18 The Impact of AI on Legal Practices
12:56 Cautionary Tales in Probate Transactions
15:23 Navigating Real Estate Transactions in Probate
17:48 Legal Implications of Improper Sales
20:33 Conclusion and Key Takeaways
23:16 Navigating Knowledge in Law and Real Estate
25:21 The Importance of Expertise in Probate Real Estate
30:57 Building Trust and Relationships in Real Estate
35:45 Advice for Personal Representatives and Executors
39:38 Demystifying the Probate Process

GUEST
Nancy Eaton, Esq., Law Office of Nancy Perry Eaton, PLLC
Website: https://www.perryeatonlaw.com/

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
In this episode of the Texas Probate Real Estate Podcast, host Jeremy Kritt sits down with award‑winning probate attorney Nancy Perry Eaton to unpack the real‑world challenges Texas families face when dealing with probate, affidavits of heirship, title issues, and investor pressure. Nancy, voted Best Attorney and Best Law Firm in the Killeen Daily Herald’s Best of Central Texas (2025), explains why Texas title companies are rejecting affidavits of heirship more frequently and how missing heirs, inaccurate affidavits, or investor‑driven contracts can jeopardize title and expose families to legal risk.

Jeremy and Nancy explain the risks of signing contracts before an executor or administrator is officially appointed, the tactics wholesalers and “We Buy Houses” companies use to pressure grieving families, and the red flags heirs should watch for. They also cover why DIY probate, online templates, and AI‑generated legal documents often lead to costly mistakes, outline the differences between independent and dependent administrations, and show how attorneys and real estate professionals work together to protect the estate’s equity.

TAKEAWAYS
-AI cannot replace professional judgment built from years of legal and real estate experience.
-DIY probate filings are risky, especially when people misunderstand statutes or court procedures.
-Some agents sign listings before an executor is appointed, creating legal exposure for the estate.
-Many agents lack probate‑specific knowledge, including authority and title requirements.
-Probate real estate requires specialized expertise, not generic real estate experience.
-Investors and wholesalers often push unauthorized deals, causing long‑term title and heirship issues.
-Experienced attorneys and brokers understand the landmines and protect the estate from costly mistakes.

WORK WITH JEREMY
Jeremy Kritt, Broker/Owner of Kritt Real Estate, Founder of Texas Probate Real Estate
Call: 512-686-3076
Website: https://www.texasprobaterealestate.com
Serving Central Texas: Travis, Hays, Williamson, Comal, Guadalupe, Bexar and Bell counties. Outside these areas? We can put you in touch with a specialist through our Texas Probate Real Estate Network.

Legal Disclaimer: This video and all content on the Texas Probate Real Estate Channel is for informational purposes only and should never be considered legal advice. Always do your own research and always consult with a licensed attorney for legal advice.

metadata.title: Title Search Explained: The Hidden Liens Investors Miss
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
A county records search only catches about 75% of the problems on a property. The other 25% are unrecorded municipal liens: water bills, code violations, and other debts tracked at the city or township level. Alex Goldovsky, founder of ProTitle USA, has spent 19 years finding what title reports miss, for everyone from small investors to Wall Street firms and Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

Alex started ProTitle during the 2008 financial crisis after a call from the FDIC, which needed help as it closed failed banks. Today his company handles a large share of title and tax reports on wholesale capital-market transactions, with human searchers on the ground in counties that still don't have online records.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Alex Goldovsky and Logan Fullmer break down how a title report can reveal your negotiating discount, which liens survive a foreclosure and which get wiped out, why a million-dollar IRS lien can sometimes be released for about $10,000, and how his curative team clears old unreleased mortgages. They also cover note investing, replacement title policies, and a DSCR loan fraud ring that bought more than 250 properties in Baltimore.

You'll learn:
- Why "more hair" on a title report can mean a bigger discount
- Which liens survive a foreclosure, and when an HOA can wipe out a first
- How IRS liens can sometimes be negotiated for pennies
- What unrecorded municipal liens are, and how to find them
- Why human searchers still beat AI for title research
- How to clear an old unreleased mortgage
- What a replacement title policy is and when note buyers need one
- How appraisal and deed fraud schemes work, and what to watch for

metadata.title: How Ex-FBI Agents Skip Trace Anyone for Real Estate Deals
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
When you can't find an heir, the deal dies. Sean and Larry Baker are retired FBI agents turned private investigators, and they help real estate investors find the people nobody else can: heirs in prison, owners living overseas, people couch surfing with no phone in their name, and people who simply don't want to be found.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Logan Fullmer and the Bakers walk through real cases from distressed property deals. They found a deported heir in a Mexican prison in days after the client had searched for months, tracked down a missionary in Uganda, and located a woman in a small town in Peru using a single Facebook account. They also share how they pulled a property from auction with four days to spare, and how a lost-dog flyer during a surveillance job ended up saving a man's life.

Whether you're skip tracing your own leads or deciding when to hire a PI, you'll learn where to look, what it costs, and how to build the sources that break a case open.

You'll learn:
- Why almost nobody is truly a "ghost," and how to find them fast
- How to find someone in jail or federal prison
- How police reports and public records can reveal phone numbers and contacts
- How investigators locate heirs overseas
- What it typically costs to hire a private investigator
- How to use surveillance and pretexts the right way
- How to turn neighbors, local shelters, and libraries into sources
- How to know when to keep digging and when to stop

metadata.title: How Matt Solved a 10 Heir Title Nightmare (A Curative Title Case Study)
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Most investors would have walked away from this one.

The property had been tied up for nearly 10 years.

There were 10 heirs spread across multiple generations, family members dragging their feet, tax delinquency issues, and just when the ownership problems appeared to be solved, four hidden life estates surfaced during title work.

In this Messy Money Case Study, curative title operator Matt Pamfilis breaks down exactly how he identified the opportunity, tracked down the heirs, negotiated ownership interests, resolved unexpected title issues, and ultimately turned a seemingly impossible situation into a nearly $100,000 deal.

If you're interested in curative title, probate, heirship issues, ownership disputes, or solving complicated Real Estate problems, this case study provides a real-world look at how experienced operators approach these opportunities.

ATTENTION:
The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: Florida Probate Explained: What Happens When Someone Dies Owning Real Estate?
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Most people think probate is simply about inheriting Grandma's house.

In reality, probate sits at the center of some of the biggest ownership questions in Florida Real Estate.

Missing heirs.
Orphaned estates.
Vacant properties.
Family disputes.
Unknown owners.
Title problems.

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, I sit down with Florida probate attorney Al Nicoletti to break down what actually happens when someone dies owning Real Estate in Florida.

We discuss how ownership transfers after death, when probate is required, when it can be avoided, how to identify the right heirs, who actually has authority to sell, and what investors need to know before pursuing probate opportunities.

Whether you're an investor, Realtor, title professional, attorney, or simply trying to understand inherited property in Florida, this episode provides a practical roadmap for navigating probate and ownership issues.

What You'll Learn:
-What actually happens to ownership when someone dies in Florida
-When probate is required and when it can be avoided
-How trusts, Lady Bird Deeds, and joint ownership affect probate
-The first questions to ask when investigating an inherited property
-How to determine whether a will exists
-How to identify heirs when probate has never been opened
-Who actually has authority to sell inherited property
-The difference between heirs, beneficiaries, executors, and personal representatives
-When heirs can sign contracts before probate
-The difference between summary administration and formal administration
-Typical probate costs and timelines in Florida
-Common mistakes that derail probate deals
-How experienced operators solve complex ownership problems

The probate process, explained for real estate agents and investors. All 12 steps from filing to the sale, and where the deals actually hide.

metadata.title: Successor in Interest and Tangled Title
metadata.author: National Housing Resource Center
metadata.shortDescription:
For many people, most of their wealth is attributed to their home. However, until a tangled title is resolved, homeowners won’t be able to take full advantage of their home’s value. The process of untangling a tangled title is often a complicated legal process that will require a cost.

In this webinar, you will hear from our panel of experts who will outline how to help your clients address successor in interest and tangled title issues.

Lisa Sitkin,  Supervising Attorney at National Housing Law Project 
Sarah Bolling Mancini, Co-Director of Advocacy at the National Consumer Law Center
Elizabeth Blosser, Vice President of Government Affairs with American Land Title Association
Carrie L. Mann, Esq., Vice President of Pennsylvania Land Title Association

metadata.title: Before You Go From Wholesaling to Curative Title, Watch This
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Thinking about making the jump from wholesaling into curative title investing?

You probably have more of a head start than you realize—but some of the habits that work in wholesaling can actually hurt you in curative title.

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, I break down what transfers from wholesaling, what you may need to unlearn, and why curative title requires a deeper level of problem solving, research, patience, and risk analysis.

We cover:

Why wholesalers aren't starting from zero
The difference between identifying problems and actually solving them
Why competency should come before scaling
Where your money is better spent in curative title
Why relying entirely on the title company can hurt you
Why speed isn't always an advantage
Why small spreads can be dangerous in curative deals
When to bring in attorneys, genealogists, investigators, and other professionals

Curative title isn't just wholesaling harder deals. It's learning how to understand messy title and ownership problems well enough to determine whether they can be solved—and whether there's enough profit to make solving them worthwhile.

ATTENTION:

The information shared in this episode is for educational and informational purposes only and reflects personal experiences and opinions. It is not intended as legal, tax, financial, or investment advice. Real Estate laws, tax rules, and regulations vary by state and situation. Always consult with a qualified attorney, CPA, or other licensed professional before making any Real Estate or financial decisions.

metadata.title: Neo4j Live: Entity Resolution and Deduplication with Neo4j and GenAI
metadata.author: Neo4j
metadata.shortDescription:
Starting with a knowledge graph constructed from unstructured data with the help of LLMs, we'll address the common challenge of duplicated entities resulting from variations in extracted names and identifiers.

Discover how Neo4j’s Node Similarity algorithms can be leveraged to identify and merge these entities, enhancing the accuracy and usability of your data.

Guest: Johannes Jolkkonen @johannesjolkkonen 

Graphstuff.FM: https://graphstuff.fm/episodes/rag-databases-with-johannes-jolkkonen-when-to-choose-a-graph-database-vs-alternative-vector-or-relational-stores 
Node Similarity: https://neo4j.com/docs/graph-data-science/current/algorithms/node-similarity/
fastRP: https://neo4j.com/docs/graph-data-science/current/machine-learning/node-embeddings/fastrp/
Entity Resolution and Deduping: Best Practices From Neo4j's Field Team https://youtu.be/O9Qpz6dI9zg

#neo4j #graphdatabase #entity #duplicate #genai #llm #knowledgegraph

metadata.shortDescription:
📜 Dive into the world of historical document digitization with our comprehensive tutorial on Transkribus. Perfect for historians and digital archivists, this video is your first step towards mastering the art of bringing ancient texts to the digital era. 🌐

⚙️ What's Inside:

Getting Started: Learn how to create your free account on Transkribus and navigate its intuitive dashboard.
Key Workspaces Explained: Discover the three main areas - the Desk, Models, and Sites workspaces - and their unique functionalities.
Uploading Documents: A guide on uploading texts in various formats and organizing them into Collections.
Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR): Explore public AI models for different languages and time periods, and learn how to train your custom model for specialized texts.
Editing and Collaboration: Tips on using the Document Editor for precise text-image synchronization and collaboration features for team projects.
Community Involvement: Find out how your participation in the READ-COOP community contributes to the enhancement of Transkribus.
Resources for Assistance: Guidance on accessing help resources including guides, FAQs.

🔍 Why Transkribus?
Transkribus is not just a tool; it's a gateway to unlocking historical narratives, preserving them for future generations. Whether you're a professional historian, a student, or an enthusiast in the field of digital archiving, this platform offers an unparalleled experience in digitizing and transcribing historical documents.

👥 Join Our Community:
Subscribe to our channel for more in-depth tutorials and become part of a growing community of digital history enthusiasts. Your journey into the past starts here!

🔗 Useful Links:

Transkribus Web App: app.transkribus.eu
Help and Support: help.transkribus.org


#TranskribusTutorial #DigitalArchiving #HistoricalDocuments #AIModelTraining #CollaborativeEditing #DigitalHumanities

metadata.title: The Basics of Forensic Investigative Genetic Genealogy
metadata.author: Allen County Public Library
metadata.shortDescription:
The 2018 arrest of Joseph D’Angelo, also known as the Golden State Killer, caused a huge stir in the genetic genealogy community. Since then, over 1000 cases involving suspect DNA or unidentified human remains have been resolved using the technique known as Forensic Investigative Genetic Genealogy (FIGG). This presentation will cover the history of this new field, give an introduction to how this technique works, discuss ethical issues stemming from this field, and a brief review of educational opportunities for those who would like to learn more.

Jennifer Wiebe is a professional genealogist. She loves solving all the different kinds of puzzles that genealogical mysteries bring. She currently teaches genetic genealogy for the University of New Haven’s Forensic Genetic Genealogy graduate certificate program, which she graduated from in 2022. While at Barbara Rae-Venter’s Firebird Forensic Group, she helped identify Unidentified Human Remains and potential suspects of violent crimes. She is a member of the Association of Professional Genealogists and a ProGen alumni, and has completed three genealogical institutes. With her career in education prior to becoming a genealogist, she enjoys educating others about genealogy through her blog, Jennealogie, and presenting at conferences. As a volunteer Search Angel, she's united adoptees with their biological families. One of her favourite places to visit is the Mount Royal Cemetery in her hometown of Montreal, Quebec.

Handout: https://static.libnet.info/frontend-images/pdfs/acpl/Genealogy/Allen_Library_Presentation_Handout.pdf

metadata.title: NODES 2024 - Beyond the Silos  Achieving Data Harmony With Graph Based ER
metadata.author: Neo4j
metadata.shortDescription:
Entity Resolution (ER) serves to interlink fragmented and dispersed data, facilitating the identification of records representing identical real-world entities. This function is pivotal for intelligence analysis, enriching investigations by ensuring comprehensive and uniform data merging.
 This session will showcase a robust end-to-end approach for precise and effective data consolidation, adaptable to batch or incremental processing and predominantly reliant on graphs. Key themes will encompass customizable similarity rules, harnessing node attributes and relationship patterns, and strategic utilization of Neo4j indexes and GDS. Additionally, we’ll delve into diverse data modeling strategies, evaluating their advantages and drawbacks and how to accommodate dynamic data changes.

With Federica Ventruto


Get certified with GraphAcademy: https://dev.neo4j.com/learngraph
Neo4j AuraDB https://dev.neo4j.com/auradb
Knowledge Graph Builder https://dev.neo4j.com/KGBuilder
Neo4j GenAI https://dev.neo4j.com/graphrag

metadata.title: Exporting Regrid Data to ArcGIS - Regrid Property App (Web)
metadata.author: Regrid
metadata.shortDescription:
Exporting data as a shapefile (.SHP) from the Regrid platform, then importing it into ArcGIS Pro.

The Regrid Property App is great if you want to see and work with property data using the tools we provide. If you are an Esri user and like our data (and especially if you have complex workfllows), you may be interested in our Feature Service product, which "streams" our property data directly into Esri platforms: https://regrid.com/feature-service

Please note that the Regrid Property App interface has been updated since this video was shot - while the UI is slightly different now, the functionality remains the same.

metadata.title: Transkribus Webinar for Beginners (English)
metadata.author: Transkribus
metadata.shortDescription:
Transkribus is the most popular tools for automatic text recognition of historical documents. 

By watching this webinar recording, you will learn how to upload documents to Transkribus, perform automatic text recognition with public AI model and use the document editor to edit the content. You will learn how to enrich your documents with tags, search for specific words and phrases and export the transcriptions in different formats. 

We also take a brief look at how you you can train your own text recognition models that are able to recognise specific fonts in your documents.

🔗 More Useful Links:
Transkribus Web App: app.transkribus.org
Help and Support: help.transkribus.org

#Transkribus #TranskribusTutorial #HowTo #GettingStarted #DigitalArchiving #HistoricalDocuments #DigitalHumanities

metadata.title: Using Datasets - Regrid Property App (Web)
metadata.author: Regrid
metadata.shortDescription:
The Regrid Property App allows you to manage datasets in your account, such as data you've imported, or data you've created in the app (for example, by Following a property, adding data to a Survey, etc). This video shows you how to work with them inside your account.

Note: this video was shot prior to an update to the Regrid Property App's interface. While the new version looks a little different, all the functionality is the same as described in the video.

metadata.title: Regrid Mapping Platform - Filter Data
metadata.author: Regrid
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn how to filter data on the Regrid Mapping Platform.

Regrid's mapping tools make working with property data easy. Filter to find properties of interest, add notes and photos to properties, and much more.

Regrid's Mapping Platform - https://app.regrid.com
Learn more - https://regrid.com/saas

Our mapping platform is great if you want to see and work with property data using the tools we provide. If you want to pull our data into your GIS software or database, please see our bulk data options below and email us at parcels@regrid.com to get set up.

metadata.title: Best Real Estate Data APIs for Building a Deal Finder App
metadata.author: REI Tech Club
metadata.shortDescription:
In this video, I take you behind the scenes of my journey to build an AI-powered deal-finding app for real estate investing. The concept is simple: scan active listings, apply my buy box, and get the best deals in my inbox every day. But the biggest challenge? Finding a reliable, legal data source—without a real estate license or access to the MLS.

I started with the obvious options like Zillow and Redfin, but scraping them is a legal minefield. I explored official MLS APIs, but most of them require licensing, bureaucracy, and enterprise-level partnerships. So I had to keep going.

Eventually, I filtered down dozens of data providers to just a few that seemed transparent, investor-friendly, and easy to work with. In the end, I chose Rentcast—a tool with open API documentation, clear pricing, and solid national coverage, even if it isn’t a direct MLS feed.

This is the first step in building a smarter real estate tool—and a smarter investing system—with AI. If you’re a solo investor or builder looking to leverage tech in your real estate strategy, this channel is for you.

Subscribe to stay updated on the build, or join the REI + AI newsletter at: https://reiplusai.com/

For business inquiries, contact: ben@reiplusai.com
keywords: how to find real estate deals
how to use ai for real estate

DataTree Discount: https://retipster.com/go/datatree/yt-ntT8V0gnpAs (REtipster Affiliate Link)

Want to use the property research spreadsheet? You can download it from the blog here: https://retipster.com/propertyresearch/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=blog&utm_content=ntT8V0gnpAs

Find out if your property has wetlands: https://retipster.com/wetlands/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=blog&utm_content=ntT8V0gnpAs

What is a "perc test" and how much does it really matter: https://retipster.com/perc-test/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=blog&utm_content=ntT8V0gnpAs

During my first few years as a real estate investor, I found that my research process was one of the biggest time-wasters I had to deal with.

Why? Because, in my mind, to feel comfortable sending out an offer on any property, I had to know everything there was to know (this was my first mistake). As a result, I spent a ton of time ensuring that I understood every possible thing about a property before making an offer. I would leave no stone unturned.

Well...   an abundance of caution isn't a bad thing per se, but I eventually figured out that this approach was hurting me.

You see -- for me to be profitable in my business... I had to close a deal every once in a while (I know, sounds crazy, right?).

Well, to close a deal, I had to get some accepted offers.

For every accepted offer I got, I usually had to send out a lot of offers, and I had to do this on an ongoing basis (not one offer per week...   but more like a DOZEN offers per week).

...if I wanted to crank out this kind of volume all by myself, it wasn't a good use of my time to spend several hours researching each property before I felt "comfortable" enough to send out one offer. The math just didn't add up! Something had to change if I wanted ANY hope of getting anywhere in this business.

Let me tell you from experience that when you're offering somebody 10% -- 30% of their property's market value (like I do), many of them will say "No." That's just part of the deal when you're fishing for motivated sellers and offering them virtually nothing for their property. A general lack of acceptance shouldn't take anybody by surprise.

Once I realized this, I knew I had to cut the fat out of my research process. I didn't have an hour or more to research every property I came across! If I didn't make some drastic changes, I wasn't going to survive as a real estate investor.

After a lot of fine-tuning and experimentation, I could whittle down my research process to what I considered to be the most important factors. These were the essential pieces of information that needed to be known for me to determine:

1. Whether Or Not To Make An Offer
2. How Much To Offer

This list of "bare essentials," i.e. -- the checklist I followed in researching each property, is outlined in the video above. #realestatewebsite #realestate #retipster #sethwilliams #realestateinvesting

When you buy a property, one of the many things you should be checking is the annual property tax expense because once you own the property, this expense will be yours to pay.

Likewise, one of the many things you or your closing agent will want to do before closing on a real estate transaction is to verify that the property taxes are paid current and not past due.

You can do both of these things with DataTree. I'll show you how it works in this video.

Of course, you can also get this information by calling your city, township, or county tax collector to verify these numbers, but DataTree makes it much easier.

metadata.shortDescription:
Kathryn Moore explains Forensic Investigative Genetic Genealogy (FIGG) and how genetic genealogy research can be used to solve criminal investigations. Learn about this unique application of genetic genealogy and how DNA research can help you in your own family history research.

For more information: https://familyhistory.lib.byu.edu/all-webinars/forensic-investigative-genetic-genealogy-where-family-history-meets-criminal-investigation

metadata.shortDescription:
A chance conversation suddenly breathes life into an inheritance case that had been shelved for years.

In this episode of Heir Hunters, probate researchers reopen the mystery of the Gagneux estate after a new lead emerges. Meanwhile in Liverpool, investigators uncover the story of an Irish family whose journey to the city began around the docks at the turn of the 20th century.

Series 10 Episode 1 — Gagneux / Wareing

Real investigations into inheritance, genealogy, unclaimed estates and the families connected to the UK’s Bona Vacantia list.

Subscribe for more true stories of lost relatives and unexpected inheritances.

#HeirHunters #Inheritance #UnclaimedEstates #FamilyHistory #Genealogy #BonaVacantia #MissingHeirs #ProbateResearch #RealStories #BBCDocumentary #FamilySecrets #UKDocumentary

metadata.title: Genealogy 301: Forensics to Find Heirs,Trace Lineage & Solve Crimes
metadata.author: AARP Ohio - The Buckeye State!
metadata.shortDescription: Forensic genealogists combine the law, finding family members listed in wills, finding birth families, locating family members for the military, even working with the police to solve crimes. Forensic genealogists solve cases using birth certificates, newspapers, even DNA. Watch as a professional forensic genealogist discusses how people-locating skills are used to find missing and unknown heirs. AARP also provides resources to help you with the joy and responsibilities of caring for your older adult family members.

segments.text: Ever since the 2018 announcement that
the Golden State Killer had been
identified using genetic genealogy, a
non-stop stream of cold cases have been
solved using the same techniques. Now,
thousands of genealogists, true crime
fans, and even people already working in
the forensic world hope to become
investigative genetic genealogists and
learn the necessary skills. But, how
does one even get a job as an
investigative genetic genealogist?
Hello, everybody. I am Joseph Ross, the
Genie Vlogger, and on today's video,
I'll be discussing how to become an
investigative genetic genealogist. I
spent about 5 years working as the lead
investigative genetic genealogist at the
company DNA Labs International, working
my first case in March of 2019.
So, I have a lot of insight into this,
and later in the video, I'll actually
discuss how I became an investigative
genetic genealogist. But first, let's
quickly define what is an investigative
genetic genealogist, or what I'll call
an IGG or IGG practitioner. This is
someone who uses genetic genealogy to
solve cold case crimes or identify
unknown human remains. IGG often gets
confused with what's known as forensic
genealogy, which is the use of genealogy
for any legal matter. So, while IGG is a
part of the forensic genealogy world,
there is much more to it than just that,
things like military repatriations,
heir research, and much more. IGG may
also be referred to as forensic
investigative genetic genealogy, or what
some people would just call FIG. And
this is the same thing as investigative
genetic genealogy, IGG, it's just some
people really wanted to try to
differentiate the the term used for
this, and there's no concise use
necessarily at this point. Some folks
use IGG, some folks use FIG, others will
just say forensic genealogy even though
they mean IGG specifically. So,
hopefully this clears up any confusion
for anyone that wasn't really quite
sure. But now let's talk about what you
actually need to become an IGG
practitioner. And at this point, there
are no requirements of any sort of
certificates or degrees to become one.
In fact, there really isn't anything
even created for that quite yet,
although there is an accreditation board
that recently came about and people can
go and get that accreditation, but it
isn't required to actually work in the
field. But as for the actual skills you
need to become an IGG practitioner,
there are many. Most importantly, and I
imagine this is fairly obvious with the
job, you have to have a very advanced
skill with both genealogy and genetic
genealogy. And this really means
experience with genealogy and genetic
genealogy across various population
groups because it's going to be very
different with each population group
that you work on. And this is honestly
one of the biggest issues and hurdles
that any non-genealogy enthusiast will
have to overcome. Basically, the people
that really want to get into this work,
but never have really built their own
family trees or really built other
people's family trees, they're just
really intrigued by the crime-solving
aspect of it and see this is kind of a
way to get in that they find
interesting. But the reality is is that
you need to have thousands of hours
doing both genealogy
and genetic genealogy. And most IGG
practitioners gain that experience from
years, if not decades, of doing their
own family trees, doing their friends'
family trees, doing the family trees of
their relatives' spouses, doing the
family trees of all sorts of people
they've met, and many even doing
professional work as genealogists. And
even beyond the actual hands-on
experience, you really also need a lot
of experience through various learning
opportunities. And this is something
most genealogists, even very experienced
genealogists, constantly do. I mean,
think of any sort of continuing
education in any industry. People are
constantly going to conferences, going
to various events where they can learn
and build their experience, as well as
keep up with the latest things going on.
First off, there's a plethora of online
content such as webinars, classes,
workshops, and just all sorts of things
that you can do just from the comfort of
your home and be able to learn all sorts
of genealogy and genetic genealogy
skills. I even have multiple clients
that I've worked with that have done
genealogy and genetic genealogy for
years and years, but they use me for
consultations to help guide them, to
help teach them, and to help them expand
their own knowledge. Speaking of which,
if anyone would be interested in having
a consultation with me, be sure to go to
my website www. .genievlogger.com and
you can book a consultation there. But
even here on YouTube, there's a ton of
content to learn, all sorts of
tutorials, even just fun videos that
show you the in and out of genealogy but
in a fun way with narratives and stuff,
such as my YouTuber family tree series
where you're basically learning the
history of a famous YouTuber's family
while also seeing how that work was
done. And something that's very
important within the genealogy community
are actually Facebook groups, which are
often the main places that a lot of the
genealogy community interacts with each
other and a lot of latest news gets
released, and it's really a place that,
ever since the beginning of Facebook
groups, has been a core part of the
genealogy world. So, an absolutely
amazing resource for anyone that's
trying to get into this field as well.
Joining these Facebook groups and being
able to connect and learn, and also it's
a place where you can help others to
gain your own experience. And beyond the
online stuff, there's also a ton of
in-person stuff from just local
genealogy society meetings where they're
maybe hosting a speaker to various
genealogy institutes that then have, you
know, full weeks of classes where every
day you're doing classes from 10:00 a.m.
until 4:00 p.m. in the afternoon,
working with all of your genealogy
buddies. And then, of course, genealogy
conferences of all various sizes. The
largest genealogy conference, RootsTech,
brings in over 20,000 people in person
every year to Salt Lake City with
millions of people accessing it online.
And it is the largest in the world by
far. But there's also a lot of smaller
genealogy conferences all over the
country and all over the world, so you
can really go and get a big connection
with both genealogists themselves and
networking, as well as educational
opportunities. I mean, in all reality,
the genealogy landscape is massive,
especially as you get into more and more
specific niches within different
population groups or migrations or
histories. There's just so much, and
there are so many different groups
geared towards each one of those pieces.
And these in-person events are also
extremely important for networking,
which is really important to establish
these working relationships with all
sorts of genealogists and genetic
genealogists, and especially folks that
are already IGG practitioners. But in
terms of skills, you will need some very
specific sorts of expertises that are
geared towards IGG work. And the
experience you need really only comes
from hands-on experience, and to do
that, you need to work what's known as
unknown parentage cases. An unknown
parentage case is just a case where
someone has unknown biological ancestry,
and so they use genetic genealogy to try
to identify that biological family. And
this includes things like adoptions,
foundlings,
uh donor conceived, or just any case
where there's unknown biological
ancestry. These types of cases use the
exact same tools and techniques that we
use in IGG cases. Now, most people that
get the experience solving unknown
parentage cases get it through doing
volunteer work. What's often called
being a search angel. And there are
actual search angel groups that you can
join. You can also do this by finding
people through some of those Facebook
groups or possible other forums. And
sometimes you can just do this
with people that you meet in person if
they're interested and you're willing to
spend the time to help them out. And I
honestly find that most people that do
search angel work will do a mixture of
all of those helping in different
Facebook groups, also getting people
through the actual search angel groups,
and even just friends of theirs, and
friends of friends in person. Now, I do
want to say here that if you plan to do
search angel work, make sure that you
already have experience with genetic
genealogy, and really an extensive
amount of experience. These cases deal
with real people, and they have real
consequences, and the last thing you
want to do is screw something up for
someone where they then are never going
to be able to meet their biological
family because of something you did.
Now, as for the actual specific
techniques and tools that you will need
to do IGG work, there are many from
things like relationship prediction
calculators to DNA match clustering, but
one of the most important techniques
that you really need to get down is
what's known as descendancy
research. And this is just the ability
to build a family tree down identifying
